subject: arts-music
essential_question: How can understanding theatre and media production help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
project_brief: Produce a short scene, audio drama, storyboard, or media piece with safe permissions and role options. This is the grade 7 culminating project for "Theatre and Media Production" (ma-g7-arts-and-music-u04, unit 4), built around character objective and obstacle, script structure, blocking and voice, camera and framing concepts, and sound and editing. Produce a short scene, audio drama, storyboard, or media piece with safe permissions and role options. Choose your own sharing format ahead of time: a private read-through with your facilitator, a recording made only for your own review, or a live audience — no format is required over another.
requirements: Address every topic listed for this unit: character objective and obstacle, script structure, blocking and voice, camera and framing concepts, sound and editing, and production roles and consent.
Meet the performance task as written: Produce a short scene, audio drama, storyboard, or media piece with safe permissions and role options.
Show your work or process, not just a final result — a process note, sketch log, commit history, or draft trail.
Complete the checklist in this package before submitting.
primary_task: Produce a short scene, audio drama, storyboard, or media piece with safe permissions and role options. Choose your own sharing format ahead of time: a private read-through with your facilitator, a recording made only for your own review, or a live audience — no format is required over another.
critique_criteria: A named viewer, listener, or reader can point to a specific choice in the work and connect it back to character objective and obstacle or another named topic from this unit.
The piece shows at least one deliberate revision — a version-two decision made because the first attempt did not achieve the intended effect.
The student can explain the intended effect on an audience in their own words, separate from just describing what was made.
Only the student's own original work, public-domain material, or a properly licensed and cited excerpt appears in the piece — no unlicensed lyrics, sheet music, or protected work is reproduced.

The submitted evidence (written account, notation, recording made for the student's own review, or live demonstration to the facilitator) is sufficient for a reviewer who was not present to judge the criteria above.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: Sharing this project publicly is always optional and never required for full credit. You may present live to a small audience of your choosing, present privately to just your facilitator, submit a recording made only for your own review, or submit a written/described account of the finished work instead.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: If any part of this task could involve singing, speaking on camera, or being recorded, you may instead notate the piece, write a detailed description or script, use body percussion or an instrument in place of your voice, or perform live for your facilitator with no recording made at all. No lesson in this unit requires a voice recording, a camera, or a photo.

copyright_and_authorship: The final submitted work must remain your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI assistant may help you plan, explain a concept, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but may not produce the graded work itself. Use only your own original work, public-domain material, or a properly licensed and cited excerpt — never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or another protected work without the rights to do so.
remediation: If the piece isn't coming together, return to a single, smaller exercise focused only on character objective and obstacle, revisit one worked example or model from this unit, and rebuild your confidence with that one element before returning to the full project.
extension: Once the core piece is finished, create a second short variation that explores script structure from a different angle, or write a short artist's statement comparing your original intent with what the finished work actually communicates.
